target_customer: Solar EPC contractors and developers building utility scale solar farms
problem: Utility solar construction is limited by scarce, expensive field labor. Charge Robotics builds a portable robotic assembly line (Sunrise) that automates structural assembly and panel installation.
business_model: Robotic factory plus trained crew sold to EPCs as a construction service (pilot program)

founders.name: Banks Hunter
education: MIT (class of 2015 per a directory profile)
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no bio; MIT detail is from a search summary of a directory profile, unverified.

founders.name: Max Justicz
founders.background_notes: YC page says formerly in EECS at MIT.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous outdoor robots must handle uneven terrain, heavy modules and tight tolerances for construction sites, a hard hardware and robotics problem.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus field operations know how and integration with EPC workflows is hard to copy, but well funded robot rivals emerged.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: AES, Sarcos with Blattner, and Terabase announced solar installation robots in 2023 to 2024, after founding; no acquisition of Charge found.

market_need_then: Utility solar build outs faced labor shortages; the company site claims its system replaces 75 percent of mechanical install labor hours (company claim).

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, tagline The Assembly Line For Solar Is Here

branding.brand_signature: The Assembly Line For Solar Is Here tagline and Sunrise factory product
branding.community_and_virality: Press from MIT News (March 2025) and Fast Company (April 2024) linked on the YC page.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear tagline and notable press, but another company named Charging Robotics exists and the brand has no standout asset.

outcome_analysis: Charge Robotics grew from a 2021 YC start to about 25 people and reports raising $17M in 2024 and $22M in March 2025 to fund first commercial deployments of Sunrise, including a partnership with SOLV Energy. It is a capital intensive hardware company that has attracted rounds, but commercial scale is still ahead.
notes: Round stage labels conflict: aggregators call the $17M a Series A (July 2024, one lists Aug 2024) and the $22M a Series B, while pv magazine only says a $22M raise. An Energies Media piece dated July 2026 also reports $22M, a conflict in date. Totals range $22M to $39M. Investors not found. Seed round led by YC mentioned in one source, amount unknown, so not recorded. Competitor list empty: the dated competitor search returned only 2023 to 2026 entrants, none near the 2021 batch.
